articles.headline: Magic's Jalen Suggs out at least 2 weeks with knee injury
articles.description: Magic guard Jalen Suggs suffered a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will miss at least the next two weeks.
articles.headlineJa: マジックのジェレン・サグス、膝の怪我で少なくとも2週間欠場
articles.descriptionJa: マジックのガード、ジェレン・サグスが右膝に軽い骨挫傷を負い、少なくとも今後2週間は欠場する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs will miss at least the next two weeks after suffering a mild bone bruise in his right knee, the team announced Monday.

Suggs will be re-evaluated in two weeks, but has avoided any major structural damage.

The noncontact injury occurred late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the New York Knicks.

Suggs was on a breakaway fast break when his right knee appeared to buckle on his layup attempt with 2:09 remaining. Suggs stayed on the floor for several moments in pain before being helped to his feet.

He walked gingerly to the Magic's locker room with help from team personnel.

Suggs, the fifth pick in the 2021 draft, has averaged 12.6 points, 3.8 assists and 3.4 rebounds over his six-year career. He battled injuries the past two years that limited him to 92 games.

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

articles.headline: Vikings RB Jones avoids serious knee injury, day-to-day
articles.description: Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. avoided a serious knee injury Sunday and is considered day-to-day, coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Monday.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスのRBジョーンズ、深刻な膝の怪我は免れる、状態は日単位で管理
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスのランニングバック、アーロン・ジョーンズ・シニアは日曜日に深刻な膝の怪我を免れた。ケビン・オコネル監督が月曜日に、状態は日単位で判断されると発表した。
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. avoided a serious knee injury Sunday and is considered day-to-day, coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Monday.

The Vikings have been connected to trade rumors involving veteran running backs for most of the season. O'Connell said he will meet this week with general manager Nolan Teasley, as he does regularly, but for now the Vikings do not anticipate a need to bolster depth at the position for the Vikings' upcoming game at the Detroit Lions.

"With where Aaron's at and where we feel coming out of the game, don't necessarily see it as a depth issue at all," O'Connell said. "But obviously things could change as we go day-to-day here."

Jones has played most of this season with a sprained MCL in his left knee and was the Vikings' primary back for four games while Jordan Mason recovered from a fractured thumb. Mason returned for Sunday's 16-10 victory over the Colts, and while Jones started and took the first four carries of the game, Mason finished with a team-high 15 carries for 68 yards.

Jones had 26 yards on eight carries, the last of which was a 17-yard scamper down the right sideline with 12:22 remaining in the fourth quarter. He absorbed a hit on the left leg from Colts safety A.J. Haulcy at the end of the run.

The Vikings entered the season planning to use rookie Demond Claiborne and veteran newcomer DeeJay Dallas behind Jones and Mason. But Claiborne has been inactive for the two games that Jones and Mason have both played in, and in the other games Claiborne and Dallas have combined for nine carries.

articles.headlineJa: 第61回スーパーボウル優勝オッズ：全32チームの優勝確率
articles.descriptionJa: 全NFLチームの勝利予想数に加え、地区優勝、カンファレンス優勝、および第61回スーパーボウル優勝のオッズ。
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs' first losses of the season had incremental ramifications on the Super Bowl odds board. San Francisco remains the favorite for the 2026 season's title at +580, but that's a lengthening from +540 the previous week. Kansas City also maintained its position in third, but lengthened from +750 to +850.

That allowed other teams to make moves up the board. The Buffalo Bills, on bye in Week 7, moved from +750 to +700 for the Super Bowl, while the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks moved into fourth place from 12-1 to 11-1 with their win over the Chiefs. The Los Angeles Rams, who were the clear title favorites until a couple weeks ago, also improved from 12-1 to 11-1 week-over-week.

Another significant mover in the futures markets was the Cincinnati Bengals, who secured a key road win over the Baltimore Ravens to become the favorites to win the AFC North (+110) for the first time this season. Cincinnati improved from 21-1 to 17-1 for the Super Bowl with the victory, while Baltimore lengthened from 10-1 to 12-1.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL awards tracker: Odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more
articles.description: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLアワード・トラッカー：MVP、新人王などの獲得オッズ
articles.descriptionJa: シーズンを通した栄誉を手にする本命は誰か？MVPや新人王などの獲得オッズを掲載する。
articles.body:
Just like the last few seasons, Joe Burrow came into the 2026 campaign as one of the top public picks to win NFL MVP. After throwing eight touchdown passes over the last two weeks, he's back in the conversation at +500, a massive improvement from 11-1 a week prior. Burrow is one of the top sportsbook liabilities for the award, according to bookmakers.

Josh Allen improved his odds to win the award (+200 to +165) on his bye week by virtue of a rare poor performance from Brock Purdy, who lengthened from +220 to +350 week-over-week. Trevor Lawrence and Patrick Mahomes, who is still the odds-on favorite for Comeback Player of the Year (-175), round out the top five at +950.

After a less-than-stellar performance against his former team, Kenneth Walker III (+280) lost favorite status for Offensive Player of the Year, trailing once and current favorite Jahmyr Gibbs (+250). Jaxon Smith-Njigba made a big move up the board in his bid to repeat as OPOY, going from +950 to +450 after a huge game in the head-to-head with Walker.

The New York Giants' upset of the Houston Texans caused John Harbaugh to rocket to the top of the Coach of the Year odds board, shortening from a sixth-best 13-1 to a favorite's +330. Todd Monken maintained second place at +400 after another win for the Cleveland Browns, while Kyle Shanahan fell from +400 to +600 after the San Francisco 49ers' first loss of the season.

Odds by DraftKings.  Super Bowl odds can be found here.

articles.headline: Dream, Valkyries to play Game 6, WNBA Finals at State Farm as Thursday matinee
articles.description: Game 6 of the WNBA Finals will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. The start time of Cavs-Hawks will be pushed back to 8 p.m. ET.
articles.headlineJa: ドリームとヴァルキリーズ、WNBAファイナル第6戦を木曜午後にステートファームで開催
articles.descriptionJa: WNBAファイナル第6戦は、木曜日の東部標準時午後12時30分からアトランタのステートファーム・アリーナで行われる。これに伴い、キャブス対ホークスの試合開始時間は東部標準時午後8時に後ろ倒しとなる。
articles.body:
After a weekend of nonstop frantic discussions and negotiation, Game 6 of the WNBA Finals will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET at 17,000-seat State Farm Arena in Atlanta.

The Atlanta Hawks-Cleveland Cavaliers game that night will move to 8:00 p.m. ET to accommodate the doubleheader, just as the Hawks did for Game 4. This allows a potential Game 7 to remain scheduled for Halloween at Chase Center in San Francisco.

All three Finals games in Atlanta have required hurried adjustments to the schedule at State Farm Arena. It took collective efforts from the WNBA, NBA, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, Dream, Valkyries and broadcast partners to figure out the best course of action again.

By moving the game earlier in the day, the WNBA avoided a scenario where a potential championship game was played inside the Dream's home arena, the 3,500-seat Gateway Center.

The other option under strong consideration was moving Game 6 to an open date at State Farm Arena on Friday and Game 7 to an open date at Chase Center on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

articles.headline: Source: Seahawks LT Charles Cross has high ankle sprain, likely to miss time
articles.description: Seahawks left tackle Charles Cross suffered a high ankle sprain and is expected to miss time, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 【情報筋】シーホークスのLTチャールズ・クロスが足関節の高位捻挫、しばらく欠場する見込み
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポートに対し、情報筋がシーホークスの左タックル、チャールズ・クロスが足関節の高位捻挫を起こし、しばらくの間試合を欠場する見込みであることを伝えた。
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks left tackle Charles Cross is expected to miss time after an MRI revealed that he suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

A source told Rapoport that the hope is Cross can return in one or two weeks.

Cross limped off the field in the fourth quarter and did not return. Josh Jones finished the game and is now in line to start the Seahawks' Week 8 game against the Chicago Bears on "Monday Night Football."

The Seahawks also lost wide receiver Rashid Shaheed to a knee injury Sunday that kept him out of the second half. On his Seattle Sports 710-AM radio show Monday, coach Mike Macdonald said, "the early returns are positive."

Macdonald also said on his radio show that the Seahawks will open up the 21-day practice window this week on rookie running back Jadarian Price, who has spent the past four games on injured reserve due to a chest injury.

Price, the team's first-round pick, is one half of their desired backfield duo along with Zach Charbonnet, who has yet to make his season debut following February ACL surgery. Charbonnet was inactive Sunday after a full week of participation in practice.

"We're sticking to our plan where he's still going to practice in a full capacity and then we'll evaluate as the week goes on and go from there," Macdonald said.

articles.headline: Man United head coach Michael Carrick leaves Carrington amid doubts over his future
articles.description: Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick has arrived at Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.
articles.headlineJa: マンUのマイケル・キャリック監督、進退を巡る不透明感の中でキャリントンを去る
articles.descriptionJa: 批判を浴びているマイケル・キャリック監督は、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのオマール・ベラーダCEOとジェイソン・ウィルコックス・フットボール・ディレクターが進退について協議した後、キャリントンに到着した。
articles.body:
Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick has left Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.

The popular former Red Devils midfielder not only steadied the ship after Ruben Amorim's rocky reign but helped it change course as his January arrival inspired the side's rise to third in the Premier League.

Carrick's impressive stint saw him rewarded with a two-year deal to stay on as United boss, but just five months later he is facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 Old Trafford loss to Bournemouth.

Talks over the managerial situation followed that defeat and continued after Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the Carrington training complex on Monday morning, the Press Association understands.

Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before 2 p.m. as United Under-21s took on Hull -- the side that helped ensure United got their Premier League season off to a nightmare start -- in a behind closed doors friendly, and left at around 5 p.m.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements for Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Carrick's side are without a win in eight games after being beaten by Bournemouth days after the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como.

United have won just two of their 12 matches in all competitions this term and their seven-point return from eight matches represents their worst start to a season since 1986.

The side sit just a point above the Premier League relegation zone in 16th place ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea, before heading into the international break with home games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Carrick sidestepped questions over his future following the Bournemouth defeat but appeared to know the writing was on the wall as he waved to the crowd and patted his chest as he exited the pitch, with fans supportively chanting his name.

The Old Trafford faithful's anger was instead aimed at the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos set-up, including United director of football Wilcox.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Monday

Who would have guessed that, at this point, last season's championship finalist New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs would be a combined 1-5?

Or that Giannis Antetokounmpo's new team, the Miami Heat, would be as winless as his old team, the Milwaukee Bucks?

Or that the Memphis Grizzlies would sit undefeated, led by the leading scorer in the NBA ... Ty Jerome?

There are nine games on the slate for tonight, three of which featuring two teams with a combined one loss. One fun matchup pits the undefeated Minnesota Timberwolves, led by the dynamic backcourt of Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball, into Cleveland to face the Cavaliers. Despite the Timberwolves leading the NBA in average scoring margin, the Cavaliers are favored to win the game. More on that, below.

The undefeated Oklahoma City Thunder are double-digit favorites over the visiting Phoenix Suns, despite the Thunder losing star wing Jalen Williams to a leg injury yesterday.

And the Houston Rockets place their unblemished record up against the visiting Atlanta Hawks, who are undefeated in their two road games to date.

Let's dig a little deeper into the slate to identify some potential fantasy streaming options and compelling betting angles.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Davion Mitchell, PG, Miami Heat (rostered in 49.4% of ESPN leagues)

Mitchell has quietly become one of the best distributors in the NBA. He has points-assists double-doubles in two of his first three games, including 22 points and 10 assists in his last outing on Saturday.

Ajay Mitchell, PG/SG, Oklahoma City Thunder (21.5%)

Mitchell will likely have a larger role moving forward after the injuries to Jalen Williams (lower leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder). As a starter last season, Mitchell averaged 14.9 PPG, 3.8 APG and 3.6 RPG in 16 games.

Jaxson Hayes, C, Utah Jazz (22.5%)

Hayes is a role player at center, but he is off to a solid start this season. He blocked six shots in his opening game against tonight's opponents, the Grizzlies. He then scored 17 points in his second game. He has five boards in all three games so far, and has totalled 10 blocks and steals in those games.

Jaylen Wells, SF/SG, Memphis Grizzlies (15.5%)

Wells has scored in mid-double figures in all three games so far, and also has totaled 14 boards, seven 3-pointers and six steals to round out his contributions this season.

Jonathan Kuminga, PF/SF, Minnesota Timberwolves (48.0%)

articles.headline: Virgil van Dijk: No one can replicate Mohamed Salah but new-look Liverpool attack has to step up
articles.description: Liverpool's revamped forward line has done well enough to ensure Mohamed Salah's name has never been mentioned at Anfield this season but captain Virgil van Dijk knows the next generation still have work to do.
articles.body:
Liverpool's revamped forward line has done well enough to ensure Mohamed Salah's name has never been mentioned at Anfield this season but captain Virgil van Dijk knows the next generation still have work to do.

Sunday's 2-0 win over Brighton was the first game in which Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz -- £364 million ($487m) of talent acquired over the last two summers -- and Cody Gakpo looked like they clicked together.

And they still had exciting 18-year-old England winger Rio Ngumoha, their gamechanger in their previous two matches, to bring off the bench.

Isak found the net for the sixth time in his last six league matches with an assist from Barcola after a deflected Wirtz shot had broken the deadlock, while there were several passages of play in which they appeared to be getting to grips with the new dynamic.

Salah departed in the summer, having cut his contract short by a year, after a disappointing campaign and although he left behind a wealth of goalscoring records -- and has scored 10 in 10 for new club Trabzonspor -- there is a general acceptance that everyone has moved on and no one is pining for the 34-year-old.

"I think it is the reality. What Mo has done for so many years as a winger, I don't think anyone can replicate that," van Dijk said.

"Hopefully it is going to happen but what he did was incredible. The same goes with Sadio [Mane] and Bobby [Roberto Firmino].

"Hopefully that is going to happen again and that is what we work for but now it is time for others and others have to step up.

"We can always think it was better back in the day but that is not the mentality that it should be at a club like Liverpool and I don't feel it has ever been.

"The club will always move on at a certain point and there are always players who will shine and perform for the club.

"It is down to these players who are here now to show it every three or four days.

"The second goal was class but there are plenty of moments already this season that they have been very good.

"At a club like Liverpool you have to do it every three or four days. That is always the challenge, but it is a nice challenge. I'm pretty confident that it is going to be fine."

Victory moved Liverpool, whose only defeat has come at home to Manchester City, into the Premier League's top four with a fourth clean sheet of the season.

- Iraola era at Liverpool finally has liftoff thanks to big-money forwards

- Brighton's Fabian Hürzeler digs at Liverpool - 'one team' tried to create

- Jermaine Pennant rescued by pet after dog attack: 'He saved my life'

A restructured defence has seen on-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo become an instant hit on the right, while £60m ($80m) arrival from Rennes, Jérémy Jacquet, aged just 21, is looking an astute signing.

"He [Jacquet] is doing very well," van Dijk added.

"He just has to keep going and let's see where the ceiling will be. I don't think it is there yet, so keep going."
